clue.text: Taking a chance, hide in the apparatus

indicators.note: the hide is placed in the apparatus, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rig is a piece of apparatus or equipment
an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: Someone gambles by hiding inside a piece of machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling or venturing on something uncertain is a synonym for chancing it.

clue.text: Vilified for seeing wickedness in an extremist

indicators.note: wickedness is placed within the extremist

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary or extremist leftist
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone is condemned for seeing evil in a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse or denounce someone is to vilify them.

clue.text: Not weighing very heavily on one's conscience?

definitions.text: Not weighing very heavily on one's conscience?

parts.words: Not weighing very heavily on one's conscience?
parts.note: a moral doubt, and also a tiny apothecaries' weight of twenty grains

explanation.definitionFit: A small qualm of conscience shares its name with a minute unit of weight.

clue.text: A woman showing obvious dissatisfaction with a couple of points

parts.note: ire is anger, displeasure shown openly
N and E, north and east, are two compass points

explanation.surface: A woman is visibly annoyed about a pair of details.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name.

clue.text: Impressive dogs are in fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Imposing dogs are trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' reads as trendy, but 'in' is part of the anagram fodder and 'fashion' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand, imposing, magnificent.

clue.text: Row following last month's failure

indicators.note: the row comes after the month, so it is placed second

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated Dec
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A quarrel after last month led to a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-off or deterioration is a kind of failing.

clue.text: He'll cheat the German out of a rise

indicators.note: the German word sits outside the rise

parts.note: der is a German word for the
up means a rise

explanation.surface: A German swindles someone out of a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dupes others is a con man or trickster.

clue.text: Peeved over news of diversion

parts.note: peeved means annoyed, cross
word can mean news, as in sending word

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about news of a traffic detour.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a pastime, an amusement.

clue.text: Dante's great work — it could be no finer

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: Dante's masterpiece — none could be finer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Sooner appear noble? That's right!

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
ie is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone appears an aristocrat sooner rather than later — correct!
explanation.definitionFit: At a former time, before now.

clue.text: Bar even reformed characters — such a bloomer

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are formed again into a new order

explanation.surface: A ban is placed on even reformed criminals — what a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is literally something that blooms, a flowering plant; 'characters' just means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant grown for its flowers.

clue.text: Public relations advance put forward

parts.note: to advance an idea is to offer it

explanation.surface: A PR department pushes forward a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender or present something for acceptance is to put it forward.

clue.text: The person looking for some conversation

definitions.text: The person looking for some conversation

parts.words: The person looking for some conversation
parts.note: reads like someone seeking a chat, but describes a deaf person who follows speech by watching mouths

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who understands speech by watching the movement of a speaker's mouth literally looks for what is said.

clue.text: Khan in disguise raising money

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Khan in disguise raising money
explanation.walkthrough: A khan is an inn for travellers in Asia, not here a ruler; 'money' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a roadside inn where caravans rest in the East.

clue.text: Pop round about a certain apprehension

indicators.note: dad goes round the word for about, enclosing it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, dad
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Father goes round worrying about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a strong fear or apprehension of what is to come.

clue.text: Low-priced muck many make a pile from

parts.note: dirt is muck
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: Many people make their fortune from cheap rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Very inexpensive, a bargain.

clue.text: What one has to go on when out of sorts

definitions.text: What one has to go on when out of sorts

parts.words: What one has to go on when out of sorts
parts.note: suggests the evidence someone works from, but describes looking pale and unwell

explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly ill or below par, often shown in a pale face.

clue.text: They don't believe a lot can be affected

definitions.text: They don't believe a lot can be affected

parts.words: They don't believe a lot can be affected
parts.note: reads as sceptics, but 'a lot' is one's lot, fate, which such people think fixed

explanation.definitionFit: People who think events are predetermined and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Put off vulgar male cleaner

parts.note: to put someone off is to deter them
gent is a colloquial, slightly vulgar, short form of gentleman

explanation.surface: A coarse man is discouraged by a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent such as washing powder.

clue.text: Put out — used badly, though obliging

indicators.note: the words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone upset at being exploited, though helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as upset; 'Put' is a link and 'out' joins 'used' as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiful and willing to serve.

clue.text: Haircut to make a heavy-weight confident

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
sure means confident

explanation.surface: A haircut to boost a big man's confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head.

clue.text: Plan to make a medical man stern

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for a doctor
aft is the rear, the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A scheme to make a doctor strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary sketch or outline.

clue.text: Article about tip-top stop set up from the middle east

indicators.note: the article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, top-notch, written AI
to bar is to stop

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about an excellent stopover in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reads the pieces upwards; A1 for first-rate is written with the letter I standing for the figure one.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or from Arabia, in the Middle East.

clue.text: The boards should get the rate adjusted

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted into another order

explanation.surface: The board of directors needs to adjust the rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boards' is the stage, as in treading the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage, the acting profession.

clue.text: Almost too nice to be used as a mixer

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter, being only almost there

explanation.surface: Something nearly too pleasant to be served as a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims both words: TOO loses its last O and NICE its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a drink used to dilute spirits, as in gin and tonic.

clue.text: Check a vile tale being broadcast

indicators.note: the letters are scattered about and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stops a nasty story being spread.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or relieve pain is to check it, curb it.

clue.text: A novice sailing man's religious centre

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A novice sailor finds a religious focus.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the focal table in a church.

clue.text: The minister set against one form of transport

parts.note: v is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The minister opposes one type of vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest.

clue.text: Love turning up weeks before Easter loaded with cash

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the word up is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the period of weeks leading up to Easter

explanation.surface: Romance comes along in Lent for someone wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich, affluent, luxurious.

clue.text: The church official wanting credit is relaxed about it

indicators.note: sat goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to have sat is to have rested or relaxed
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church official who lacks credit doesn't worry about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrist is a sacristan, responsible for a church's vessels and vestments.

clue.text: A guy soaking can be more difficult to deal with

definitions.meaning: someone who soaks things, letting them steep
comparative of a word meaning hard, as of a slope or a price

explanation.definitionFit: One who soaks is a soaker; harder going is more precipitous or excessive.

clue.text: Foreign holy man needing cattle-grazing

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
a range is open land where cattle graze

explanation.surface: An alien holy man needs pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien or unfamiliar, from outside.
